_comment: Gate for harness/execute.py. Floors sit a little under what is observed (duckdb ~162, postgres ~66) on purpose: non-determinism is DETECTED by running both sides several times and seeing whether each agrees with itself, which is sampling, so a statement near the edge lands in 'nondeterministic' on one run and 'agree' on the next. A real regression is a cliff, not a wobble.

known_divergences.note: sqlglot reads DuckDB's omitted slice bound as -1, turning a reversal into a one-element slice. See docs/upstream-issues.md. NOT worked around: the port reproduces the reference on purpose.

sqlglot rewrites PostgreSQL's binary INTEGER literal into a BIT STRING: 10 becomes '1010'. It runs, and the value is wrong. See docs/upstream-issues.md. NOT worked around: the port reproduces the reference on purpose.

known_divergences.why: does not run: "_" is not a valid hexadecimal digit
known_divergences.note: Same class as 0b1010: the hex integer literal becomes a bit string, which rejects the _ separator. See docs/upstream-issues.md. NOT worked around: the port reproduces the reference on purpose.

known_divergences.written: SELECT EXTRACT(epoch FROM CAST('2023-01-04 04:05:06.789' AS TIMESTAMP))
known_divergences.note: DATE_PART returns double precision, EXTRACT returns numeric. Equal numbers, different type. See docs/upstream-issues.md. NOT worked around: the port reproduces the reference on purpose.

known_divergences.written: SELECT EXTRACT(CAST('isodow' AS VARCHAR(6)) FROM CURRENT_DATE)
known_divergences.why: does not run: syntax error at or near "CAST"
known_divergences.note: EXTRACT takes an identifier for its field, not a value, so the rewrite does not run at all. See docs/upstream-issues.md. NOT worked around: the port reproduces the reference on purpose.

date_add returns timestamptz; the + rewrite returns timestamp. Different behaviour across a zone boundary. See docs/upstream-issues.md. NOT worked around: the port reproduces the reference on purpose.

known_divergences.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT ARRAY[1, 2, 3] AS col) SELECT * FROM t WHERE 1 <= ANY(col) AND 2 = ANY(col)
known_divergences.written: WITH t AS (SELECT ARRAY[1, 2, 3] AS col) SELECT * FROM t WHERE FALSE
known_divergences.note: sqlglot's range rule reads `1 <= ANY(col)` as `column OP constant` and concludes two satisfiable comparisons contradict. The reference folds this identically. See docs/upstream-issues.md. NOT worked around.
